## Question 1 
To estimate the average weight of all Chihuahuas, we took a random sample with replacement of 1,000 Chihuahuas from around the world, weighed them, and calculated the average weight to be 3.9 pounds. We report a 95\% confidence interval of [3.6, 4.2]. Which of the following is true? Select all that apply.  
\begin{itemize}
\item (a) There is a 95\% chance that the average weight of all Chihuahuas in the world is between 3.6 and 4.2 pounds. \\
\item (b) If we repeated this procedure many times, 95\% of the intervals calculated this way will include the mean weight of all Chihuahuas in the world.\\
\item (c) The interval [3.6,4.2] corresponds to the middle 95\% of the bootstrap estimated sampling distribution. \\
\item (d) There is a 95\% chance the average weight of all Chihuahuas in the world is 3.9 pounds. 
\end{itemize}

## Question 2
Below is a proof using properties/rules of expectations. Select the correct rule being used at each point. 

Prove that $\hat{\mu} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i$ is unbiased for the population mean $\mu$: $E[\hat{\mu}] = \mu$


\begin{tabular}{l l }

$E[\hat{\mu} ] = E[\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i]$ & take expectation of estimator\\
& \\
$ \frac{1}{n} E[ \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i]$ &  (a) Constant Rule \\
 & (b) Linearity of Expectations \\
 & (c) Irrelevant Conditioning \\
 & (d) Law of Iterated Expectations \\
$ \frac{1}{n} E[ Y_1 + Y_2 + Y_3 + ... + Y_n]$ & \\
& \\
$ \frac{1}{n}( E[ Y_1] + E[Y_2] + E[Y_3] + ... + E[Y_n])$ &  (a) Constant Rule \\
 & (b) Linearity of Expectations \\
 & (c) Irrelevant Conditioning \\
 & (d) Law of Iterated Expectations \\
 & \\
$\frac{1}{n}( E[ Y] + E[Y] + E[Y] + ... + E[Y])$ (n times) & Y's are IID\\
& \\
$ \frac{1}{n}(\mu + \mu + \mu + ... + \mu)$ (n times) & by definition \\
& \\
$\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \mu$ & \\ 
& \\
$\frac{1}{n} n\mu$ & \\ 
& \\
$=\mu$ & \\

\end{tabular}
